answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks by enforcing slashable stake escrows across a tiered deposit terrace. Before accessing the execution wharf, each agent must sign a time-locked collateral contract using its private cryptographic quill. This imposes a verifiable opportunity cost of scarce locked capital per active identity, preventing zero-cost account replication. However, high capital requirements exclude underfunded participants and fail to deter well-financed adversaries.
